resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) for a residential resale
resale_co.issued_by: City of Englewood Building & Code Enforcement (CCO Inspector / Chief Inspector)
resale_co.lead_time: The City calls to schedule an inspection within 10 business days of receiving a complete application; the certificate is emailed 2 business days after a passed inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: If the buyer changes 30 days after the inspection, a new application and payment are needed.
requirements: All outstanding permits must be closed before the CCO inspection can be scheduled; applications are returned if there are open permits or violations
Inspection of walls, floors, ceilings, stairs and rails; no illegal apartments, illegally rented rooms or work done without permits

Smoke alarm on each level including the basement and outside each sleeping area (10-year sealed battery units, hardwired not replaced with battery); photoelectric if a bedroom is within 10 feet of the kitchen
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of the sleeping areas when there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage
ABC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)

House number at least 3 inches high in contrasting colors near the front door; no keyed deadbolt inside; bedroom egress windows open easily; handrails on 4 or more steps; bathroom fan where there is no window; water heater relief pipe within 6 inches of the floor
Central-station fire alarm systems must be tested before the inspection with a test report
Resale-only (buyer not occupying): buyer's notarized letter; bank-owned: copy of contract or notarized bank letter

fees.label: CCO application, 1 and 2 family house or condo
CCO processing/inspection, one- or two-family home (City web page)
fees.quote: The fee for processing/inspection is $150 for One- or Two-Family homes and $250 for Multi-Family homes.

resale_co.how_to_apply: The seller, seller's agent or seller's attorney completes the Residential Resale CCO application and brings or mails it with a check or money order payable to the City of Englewood to the Building Department, 2-10 N. Van Brunt St (2nd floor), Englewood, NJ 07631. Credit cards, fax and email are not accepted. Fees are non-refundable.

evidence.quote: The seller must receive a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) before transferring ownership.

City Of Englewood Revised General Ordinances Chapter 9 Article 6 ordinance Number 85-40 mandates issuance of a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) for residential properties sold in the City of Englewood.
Any outstanding permits that have been issued for work that has been done on the property must be closed out before a CCO inspection can be scheduled.
YOU WILL RECEIVE A CALL TO SCHEDULE AN APPOINTMENT WITHIN (10) BUSINESS DAYS FROM THE DATE THAT THE COMPLETED APPLICATION IS RECEIVED.
IF THE PROPERTY PASSES INSPECTION, THE CERTIFICATE WILL BE EMAILED (2) BUSINESS DAYS AFTER PASSING THE INSPECTION
IF THE BUYER CHANGES (30) DAYS AFTER THE INSPECTION, A NEW CCO APPLICATION & PAYMENT MUST BE RESUBMITTED.
Jahvia Griffin CCO Inspector CCO Inspector Email Jahvia Griffin 201-871-6650

resale_co.notes: The City page cites Ordinance 85-40; the application form says the seller agrees to Chapter 159 of the City code. The CCO inspector's email is a mailto link in the City staff directory (Building & Code Enforcement). Other contacts there: Walter Deptuch, Construction Official, 201-871-6649; Eric Dolphy, Housing & Property Maintenance Supervisor, 201-871-6646. A separate Certificate of Rental Occupancy applies to rentals and is not a sale item.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement and outside each sleeping area; 10-year sealed battery units, or hardwired; alarms over 10 years old replaced
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of each sleeping area when there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage (battery, hardwired or plug-in)
Fire extinguisher 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted, serviced and tagged within 12 months or with a recent receipt (CCO form still lists it)

authorities.name: City of Englewood (Building & Code Enforcement for the smoke/CO check during the CCO; Englewood Fire Department Fire Prevention is the LEA)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many business days before the inspection the request is made: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee.

fees.label: Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm compliance, request more than 10 business days before inspection
fees.quote: Requests made more than ten (10) business days prior to inspection: $150.00

fees.label: Request 4 to 10 business days before inspection
fees.quote: Requests made four (4) to ten (10) business days prior to inspection: $175.00

fees.label: Request fewer than 4 business days before inspection
fees.quote: Requests made fewer than four (4) business days prior to inspection: $200.00

fees.label: Reinspection fee per occurrence (ordinance spells it 'Reinsertion')

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher check is part of the CCO inspection by the City's Building & Code Enforcement office (2-10 North Van Brunt St). Ask the office whether the smoke certificate fee is charged in addition to the CCO fee.

evidence.quote: B. Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm compliance:
Penalty for failure to obtain a Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm compliance:
At least one operating smoke detector in place on each level of any living space on the property
ALL INSPECTIONS SHALL COMPLY WITH THE CURRENT STATE LAWS GOVERNING SMOKE DETECTORS, CARBON MONOXIDE ALARMS & FIRE EXTINGUISHER.
Matthew Kansky Fire Inspector Fire Inspector Email Matthew Kansky 201-871-6656

0215 Englewood City LEAID: 0215-001 Enf Auth. Fire Dept Fire Official Rocco Carbone Smoke Detector Compliance Name: Englewood City Code Enf Addr: 2-10 North Van Brunt St. Phone (201) 871-6642 Email carbone@englewoodfire.com

fire_cert.notes: Ordinance #25-53 (amending Code Section 212-17, adopted December 16, 2025, read from the ecode360 laws PDF) sets the smoke/CO certificate fees. The state fire directory names Englewood City Code Enforcement (2-10 North Van Brunt St, (201) 871-6642) as the smoke detector compliance office, and the City's CCO inspection checks the smoke and CO alarms, so the certificate appears to come with the CCO; whether both the $150 CCO fee and the smoke fee are charged is not stated. Fire Official Rocco Carbone is at the Fire Department, 81 S. Van Brunt St, (201) 871-6693. The CCO form (Rev 3/2022) still lists a fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed from the sale certificate in February 2025.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: All open permits must be closed before the CCO inspection is scheduled; applications with outstanding permits or violations are returned.

other_items.label: Illegal units
other_items.detail: Illegal apartments or unpermitted work must be removed or legalized and pass a second inspection before the CCO is issued.

open_questions: Is the smoke/CO certificate fee from Ordinance 25-53 charged on top of the $150 CCO fee, or is it included?
Does Englewood still require the fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
Is there a CCO reinspection fee?
